extracted.intended_audience: MathOverflow users who ask or tag questions about history, philosophy, biographies, education, or recreational/communication aspects of mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for MathOverflow users on when to apply the ho.history-overview tag and where history-related questions belong (MathOverflow vs HSM.stackexchange).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ho.history-overview tag
rubrics_metrics.description: History and philosophy of mathematics, biographies of mathematicians, mathematics education, recreational mathematics, communication of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tag is dedicated to the listed topics (history and philosophy of mathematics; biographies; mathematics education; recreational mathematics; communication of mathematics). Use this tag for questions touching these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer HSM.SE for history of people
rubrics_metrics.description: There is also a sister site https://hsm.stackexchange.com/, and many questions about history are more on-topic there, especially if they involve the history of people rather than that of concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a history question focuses on the history of people (biographies, careers, personal historical details), consider posting on HSM.stackexchange instead of MathOverflow. Evaluate whether the question is about historical concepts (which may fit here) or about people (often better on HSM). Note: which site is best can be controversial among users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag synonym
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tag 'history' is a synonym of ho.history-overview — use accordingly when tagging relevant questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic boundary guidance / community controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Which of the two is the best site to post history questions is a controversial topic among our users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about site choice or tag applicability, be aware there is active community debate; consider the question's focus (people vs concepts), consult site-specific help/Meta, or ask on MathOverflow Meta for guidance.
